AEM consolidation at Citi Bank Group

The recommendation

A shared organizational context, with programs aligned to delivery needs

Citi Bank Group can evaluate consolidating its Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) footprint under one Adobe IMS organization, while using multiple AEM Cloud Manager programs to organize distinct business domains or workloads.

This approach provides a shared organizational context for Adobe identity and administration, while allowing AEM delivery to be organized into separate programs where teams need different environments, repositories, pipelines, or release schedules. Adobe's AEM architecture supports multiple programs within a tenant, also referred to as an IMS organization, subject to the customer's licensing entitlements.

Sources: AEM as a Cloud Service architecture · Production program options

The operating model

Define the organization, programs, and environments as distinct layers

LayerPurpose
Citi IMS organization The shared Adobe organizational context for identity and administration.
AEM Cloud Manager programs Organize AEM workloads that benefit from distinct environments, delivery operations, or release schedules.
Environments Support each program's development, staging, and production needs, as applicable to its configuration and entitlements.

Cloud Manager programs represent logical groupings of AEM environments and initiatives. Production program availability and solution options are defined by the customer's agreement with Adobe. See production program options.

The rationale

Keep administration shared; make program boundaries intentional

Operating context

A shared organizational context

Bring the proposed AEM program structure under one IMS organization, subject to Citi's identity, administration, and governance requirements.

Delivery model

Program-level flexibility

Create separate programs where business domains have distinct delivery teams, codebases, environments, or release schedules.

Program design

A right-sized program structure

Avoid creating a separate program for every site by default. Group experiences where shared code, content, teams, and release processes make sense.

Assets strategy

An intentional Assets model

A combined Sites-and-Assets program may be appropriate when most assets support the Sites implementation and the same team manages both. A separate Assets program may be appropriate when asset workflows, teams, or lifecycle differ.

Source: Introduction to Production Programs — Program creation options.

The target-state illustration

One IMS organization can contain multiple AEM programs

The program names and count below are illustrative. The final structure should reflect Citi's business and technical requirements, as well as its licensed program and solution entitlements.

The diagram should show one Citi IMS organization above distinct Cloud Manager programs. Do not represent program cards as regulatory, legal, or data-residency boundaries.

The design principles

Use operating requirements to determine program boundaries

  1. Create programs where they support a clear operating need.

    Examples include different release schedules, delivery teams, code ownership, or environment requirements.

  2. Plan shared code and content deliberately.

    Decide which experiences should share components, content models, assets, and authoring workflows before setting program boundaries.

  3. Define access governance.

    Establish administrator responsibilities, user groups, program access, and AEM content permissions. Cloud Manager custom permissions can be configured to restrict access to programs, pipelines, and environments.

    Source: Cloud Manager custom permissions.

  4. Validate Citi's control requirements.

    Confirm with Citi stakeholders that the proposed IMS and program structure aligns with applicable legal, regulatory, security, and data-residency requirements. The proposal should not assume that multiple programs, by themselves, satisfy those requirements.

  5. Confirm entitlements before finalizing the design.

    The number and type of production programs and available solutions depend on Citi's agreement with Adobe.

The recommended next step

Align architecture and governance before setting program boundaries

Hold an architecture and governance workshop with Citi stakeholders to map business domains, delivery teams, content and code reuse, access requirements, and licensed entitlements.

Use the findings to confirm program boundaries and develop a target-state diagram and phased implementation plan.
